title: Llegar a ser: The Long Road

sections.content: You know *llegar a ser* from B1 Unit 39: the high point of a long effort (*llegó a ser presidente de la compañía*). At B2 you use it in more places. Like any verb, it can follow *querer* or *poder* (*quiero llegar a ser*, *puede llegar a ser*), and it can also describe a thing that grows into something important: *La tienda llegó a ser una gran empresa*. It always carries the idea of a path: time, effort and steps. That is the difference from *convertirse en* (the thing becomes completely new) and from *hacerse* (you simply become, with no sense of a high point). In this lesson *llegar a* always comes with *ser*.

sections.title: Ways to say "become"
rows: My uncle became mayor. (he simply became it)
Mi tío llegó a ser alcalde.
My uncle ended up as mayor. (after a long road)
La tienda llegó a ser una gran empresa.
The shop grew into a big company. (steps over time)
La estación se convirtió en un hotel.
The station became a hotel. (a complete change)

items.spanish: Quiero llegar a ser una buena cocinera.
items.english: I want to become a good cook.

items.spanish: Con el tiempo, llegó a ser muy famoso.
items.english: With time, he became very famous.

items.spanish: Puede llegar a ser un gran músico.
items.english: He could become a great musician.

sections.content: Do not use *llegar a ser* for a quick or passing change: you do not *llegar a ser pálido*, you *se pone pálido*. It also needs the road to be long enough: it fits a career, a business or a city, not a mood.
